result.topic_en: Derivation of the differential of the arithmetic-geometric mean M(x,y) by an infinite, rapidly converging series built from the successive terms of the AGM algorithm, with formulas suited to logarithmic computation.
result.transcription:
17.
$f'' = f' + \frac{1}{2}g'\frac{x'-x''}{x''}$, $f''' = f'' + \frac{1}{2}g''\frac{x''-x'''}{x'''}$ etc. Perinde fit
$g' = \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{\partial x}{x'} - \frac{\partial x}{x} + \frac{\partial y}{x'} - \frac{\partial y}{y}\right) = \frac{1}{2}\frac{\partial x}{xx'}(x-x') + \frac{1}{2}\frac{\partial y}{yx'}(y-x') =$
$\frac{1}{2}g\left(\frac{x-x'}{x'}\right)$; eodemque modo $g'' = \frac{1}{2}g'\frac{x'-x''}{x''}$, $g''' = \frac{1}{2}g''\frac{x''-x'''}{x'''}$ etc. Nec
non hinc patet esse $f' = f + g'$, $f'' = f + g' + g''$, $f''' = f + g' + g'' +$
$g'''$ etc. Nullo negotio perspicitur, seriem $\frac{g'}{g}, \frac{g''}{g}, \frac{g'''}{g}$ etc. celerrime
infra omnes limites decrescere, quamobrem habebimus per seriem
infinitam rapidissime convergentem
$f^\infty = f + g \times \{ [-\ldots-]\ \frac{1}{2}\frac{x-x'}{x'} + \frac{1}{4}\frac{x-x'}{x'}\cdot\frac{x'-x''}{x''} + \frac{1}{8}\frac{x-x'}{x'}\cdot\frac{x'-x''}{x''}\cdot\frac{x''-x'''}{x'''} + \text{etc.}\}$
$g^\infty = 0$; hinc $\frac{2\partial x^\infty}{x^\infty} = \frac{2\partial y^\infty}{y^\infty} = \frac{2\partial M(x,y)}{M(x,y)} = \frac{\partial x}{x} + \frac{\partial y}{y} + \left\{\frac{\partial x}{x} - \frac{\partial y}{y}\right\} \times \{ +$
$[-\ldots-]\ \frac{1}{2}\frac{x-x'}{x'} + \frac{1}{4}\frac{x-x'}{x'}\cdot\frac{x'-x''}{x''} + \text{etc.}\}$ sive
$\partial M(x,y) = M(x,y) \times \left\{ \begin{array}{l} \frac{\partial x}{x} \times \left(\frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{4}\frac{x-x'}{x'} + \frac{1}{8}\frac{x-x'}{x'}\cdot\frac{x'-x''}{x''} + \text{etc.}\right) \\ + \frac{\partial y}{y} \times \left(\frac{1}{2} - \frac{1}{4}\frac{x-x'}{x'} - \frac{1}{8}\frac{x-x'}{x'}\cdot\frac{x'-x''}{x''} - \text{etc.}\right) \end{array} \right\}$

Calculum aliquantum commodiorem nanciscimur sequenti modo:
Fit $\frac{x-x'}{x'} = \frac{x-y}{x+y} = \frac{(x-y)^2}{xx-yy} = \frac{(x+y)^2 - 4xy}{xx-yy} = 4\frac{x'x'-y'y'}{xx-yy}$ *) unde promanat
$\partial M(x,y) = \frac{M(x,y)}{2(xx-yy)} \times \left\{ \begin{array}{l} \frac{\partial x}{x} \times (xx-yy + 2(x'x'-y'y') + 4(x''x''-y''y'') + 8(x'''x'''-y'''y''') \ldots \\ \frac{\partial y}{y} \times (xx-yy - 2(x'x'-y'y') - 4(x''x''-y''y'') - 8(x'''x'''-y'''y''') \ldots \end{array} \right.$

Ut computus maxima facilitate per logarithmos confici possit: sequen-
tes formulas adiicimus, ex algorithmo serierum I. II sponte demanantes:
$(x'x'-y'y') = \frac{(xx-yy)^2}{16x'x'}$, $x''x''-y''y'' = \frac{(x'x'-y'y')^2}{16x''x''}$ etc., quae simul
protinus ostendunt, quanta velocitate series nostrae convergere de-
beant.

Si magis arridet, etiam sequentes formulae poterunt adhiberi:
$x'x'-y'y' = \frac{1}{4}(x-y)^2$, $x''x''-y''y'' = \frac{1}{4}(x'-y')^2$ etc.

*) et perinde $\frac{x'-x''}{x''} = 4\frac{x''x''-y''y''}{x'x'-y'y'}$, $\frac{x''-x'''}{x'''} = 4\frac{x'''x'''-y'''y'''}{x''x''-y''y''}$ etc.
